lines.text: Back to the crooked camera. Call its angle error epsilon. The tag is d meters away.
The sideways error is the far side of a thin triangle: d times the tangent of epsilon.
The tangent of one degree is zero point zero one seven five. So one point seven centimeters per meter, and three and a half at two meters.
The tag also looks turned one degree, so the goal swings about a centimeter and the robot faces one degree wrong.
Write each photo as truth plus bias plus noise. Averaging shrinks the noise toward zero, but the bias stays, every single time.
In our simulator, a misplaced element no longer hurts. But a camera turned zero point eight degrees drops success to about ninety three percent.
And a one degree bias in the camera's own tag solve drops it to about eighty. Now the camera is the error.
